title: How a recorded prison call led cops to a horrifying discovery inside a freezer in a Marrickville home
text:
By Padraig Collins for Daily Mail Australia
Published: 11:43 GMT, February 9, 2025 | Updated: 11:49 GMT, February 9, 2025
A recorded prison phone call has led to the gloomy discovery of the fetus of a baby inside a freezer inside Sydney inside.
Corrective services staff intercepted the call between an inmate and a woman abroad talking about the remains stored in a bag in a freezer in a Marickville house.
Prison officers alerted the NSW police, who raided the house last Thursday after consultations.
“After executing a court order in the house, the detectives located a bag in the freezer that contains what is believed to be a fetus,” a police spokesman Mail Australia told the police.
“A crime scene was established, and the fetus was taken to Glebe Morgue for a more detailed exam.”
Frazer Street’s house where the remains were found is understood that it is not that of the baby’s mother.
“After the exam, the police have been informed that the fetus is less than 20 weeks of gestation,” added the spokesman.
Strike Force Canfield was launched to investigate the incident.

After executing a court order at the house, the detectives located a bag in the freezer that contains what is believed to be a fetus (stock image)
As the fetus was still in the first quarter, the consultations now focus on supporting the baby’s mother.
“(There is no more police investigation (and) appropriate references (they are being made),” said the spokesman.
It is understood that the investigation is looking at a possible link between the fetus in Marrickville and the discovery of an umbilical cord and placenta last May.
That finding, by a dog walker on the Cooks river in Earlwood, was then determined by the forensic tests of a child.
The location where the placenta was found is only 3 km where the fetus was found in Marrickville.
Neither the mother or baby of the Earlwood case have been identified, although the police launched multiple public appeals to obtain information.
